title: Architect a brownfield point-solution estate into one VCF 9.1 fleet
prompt:
We need an executable architecture for the separately managed VMware estate in `fixtures/estate.json`, not an explanatory report. Build the `vcfarch` Go package and its `cmd/vcfarch` generator so that `go run ./cmd/vcfarch -inventory fixtures/estate.json -compatibility compatibility/pinned-compatibility.json` writes the JSON architecture to standard output, and commit that output as `architecture.json`. The package data model is fixed in `vcfarch/types.go` and the `Build` stub is in `vcfarch/architecture.go`; implement it without adding third-party Go modules.

Before changing the implementation, use the harness's real network research tools to search for and fetch Broadcom's currently published compatibility, interoperability, release, and upgrade-path material for vCenter, ESXi/vSAN, NSX, Live Site Recovery (including its successor in VCF 9.1), and VCF 9.1. Do not use search snippets as evidence: open the sources you rely on. In `research.md`, use a Markdown table with `Source`, `URL`, `Accessed`, and `Decision informed` columns; give every opened source an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` access date and the architecture decision it informed. The research is required even though verification is deliberately offline; do not replace live research with the pinned snapshot. If a live source has changed from the pinned authority, note the discrepancy in `research.md` but implement the pinned contract.

`architecture.json` is the machine-checkable deliverable. It must contain `schemaVersion`, `estateId`, `targetBundle`, `greenfield`, and `migrationPlan`. `greenfield` must be a greenfield VCF `SddcSpec` valid against the `SddcSpec` schema in `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, copied from tag `9.1.0.0` of the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Design a four-host vSAN ESA management domain, three NSX managers, separate MANAGEMENT/VMOTION/VSAN networks, and a single VDS; deploy new vCenter and NSX instances rather than importing the point solutions. Use the target bundle from the fixture.

`migrationPlan` must validate against `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`. It must be an ordered plan containing exactly one step for every component in the estate inventory. Every step must name the inventory component id, kind, display name, source version, target version, strategy, and all of its compatibility gates. Ordering, targets, strategies, and gates come from `compatibility/pinned-compatibility.json`, which is the stable grading authority. In particular, the standalone vCenter express patch is newer than the target base bundle: do not model its move as an in-place upgrade or downgrade. Produce a parallel-foundation migration that preserves the required component ordering and transitions Live Site Recovery to the target product named by the snapshot.

The fixture, pinned compatibility snapshot, installer specification and provenance, migration-plan schema, verifier, and `vcfarch/architecture_test.go` are protected inputs. Do not edit them. Keep tests table-driven and make `python3 verifier/verify.py` pass; it validates the `SddcSpec` against the installer specification before performing any other acceptance checks, checks the research record offline, then runs `go test -race -timeout 30s ./...` and confirms the generator reproduces the committed artifact.
